sections.html:
No Nebraska county is bigger than Douglas, whose seat and largest city is Omaha. The 2020 census counted 584,526 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 606,460. Ralston, Valley and Bennington are also cities in the county, and Boys Town and Waterloo are villages. Omaha's Elkhorn and Millard areas are part of the city.

Taxes depend on where the house sits. School districts, community colleges, cities, the county and natural resource districts each set a budget, so the district your house falls in changes its tax rate. The Assessor/Register of Deeds also watches sale prices, because every sale is recorded in the same office. Each price is compared with the last assessed value, and when prices in an area move a lot, a revaluation follows. A house that sells far from its assessment is a signal the office reads.

sections.h2: Who to call about property tax
sections.html:
Value, protests and collection sit with three separate offices: the Assessor/Register of Deeds, the Board of Equalization and the Treasurer.

  • Treasurer: (402) 444-7103, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.; mail to PO Box 2855, Omaha, NE 68103.
  • Assessor, value questions: (402) 444-7060 or valuationissues@douglascounty-ne.gov.
  • Board of Equalization: (402) 444-6510 or Protest@douglascounty-ne.gov.

The Treasurer's real property page lists payment routes: in person (cash, check, money order or card with fees), a drop box for checks and money orders, by phone with a card, online by card, PayPal or e-check at $1.50, and by mail. The Assessor controls the mailing address on file, not the Treasurer, so use the Assessor's form to change it and keep statements coming.

Statements go out in December and all tax is due by December 31, though a bill isn't late until later. Nebraska Revised Statute 77-204 makes the first half late on April 1 and the second on August 1.

Date or ruleDouglas County detail
DecemberStatements mailed
December 20If no statement has arrived, email Customer Service with the parcel number or address
December 31All taxes due
April 1First half late
August 1Second half late
Delinquent interest14% a year, accruing daily (section 77-207)

Ahead of closing, ask for a payoff for the exact closing day, because interest accrues daily and a figure from last week will be off. The Treasurer offers an online delinquency estimator, which needs the total tax from the property search.

Nebraska taxes are paid in arrears. In the Board of Equalization's words, the tax you pay in calendar year 2026 is your 2025 tax, based on your 2025 valuation. Your 2026 valuation affects the bill you pay in 2027, so a buyer inherits the next valuation, not the one on today's statement.

Overpayments can be refunded if the request is filed within three years of the tax due date (section 77-1734.01). The office refunds the payer, such as a title or mortgage company.

The formal protest goes to the Board of Equalization between June 1 and June 30. Owners who think the value is above market can also use an informal hearing window, January 15 to February 1, described in the Assessor's FAQ.

The BOE protest page explains the process:

  • Online filing opens June 1 and closes at 11:59 p.m. on June 30.
  • Mailed protests must be postmarked by June 30.
  • Hand delivery is accepted until 6 p.m. on June 30, when the office stays open late.
  • A referee appointment is optional, runs about 15 minutes, and can be in person or by phone.
  • USB drives and discs aren't accepted, and photos become public record.

Nebraska law lets anyone file a protest on any property. If the signer isn't the owner and has no authorization, the owner is notified by mail. State law requires homes to be valued at actual market value, which the Assessor defines as the likely price the property would sell for.

Real estate with delinquent taxes can go to a county auction of tax lien certificates. The Treasurer's tax sale page explains that investors buy a lien for unpaid taxes, interest and costs, not the property itself.

  • The Public Tax Sale is online, on the first Monday in March.
  • Advertising starts the first Thursday in February and runs three weeks.
  • To stay out of the ad, pay delinquent taxes by the last Wednesday in January.
  • A Private Tax Sale follows in May, and a Subsequent Tax Sale in mid-September.
  • Owners can redeem within 3 years from the date of sale by paying taxes, interest and fees.

The January payment deadline lands before the ads run, so an owner behind on taxes has a short window to clear the balance or arrange a sale.

sections.h2: Deed recording and the stamp tax
sections.html:
Your deed is filed with the Assessor/Register of Deeds, and the state's documentary stamp tax comes due. For deeds recorded from July 18, 2026 the Department of Revenue lists $3.32 on every $1,000 of value. The grantor, the seller, is liable, though the buyer or any agent presenting the deed may pay it.

The register stamps each recorded deed, and the sale data from those recordings is what the Assessor then uses to study the market. A gift or an estate deed may qualify for an exemption on the Department of Revenue's published list.

sections.h2: Selling a Douglas County house with back tax
sections.html:
Back tax, an open protest or an old lien won't block a sale. Your title company requests payoffs from the Treasurer, pays them from your proceeds and records the deed. Send Cash Home Buyers a Douglas County address in that situation and we'll explain how an as-is offer works. Saying no costs nothing.

Before you list, collect your latest statement, the parcel number, confirm whether a first or second half is late, and decide if a June 30 protest makes sense or whether a sale will move the next valuation to the buyer. If a delinquent parcel is heading toward the February ad, aim to close before the last Wednesday in January.

Also decide who will present the deed and pay the stamp tax, and how the current-year bill is split with the buyer. These two items are settled at the table, and having them written down avoids an argument over a few lines on the settlement statement. If a protest is pending, tell the title company and the buyer so nobody is surprised by a later change in value. Keep your Treasurer, Assessor and Board of Equalization numbers handy through closing day. If you move before the sale closes, update your mailing address with the Assessor right away so the bill and any notices still reach you, and forward anything that arrives to the title company.

faqs.q: When is Douglas County, NE property tax due?
faqs.a: Statements arrive in December and all taxes are due by December 31. April 1 is the late date for the first half, and August 1 for the second.

faqs.q: What is the Douglas County property tax protest deadline?
faqs.a: June 30. The formal protest period runs June 1 to June 30, and mailed protests need a June 30 postmark.

faqs.q: What interest does Douglas County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: The rate is 14% a year under Nebraska statute 77-207, and interest accrues daily.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem after a Douglas County tax sale?
faqs.a: Owners can redeem within 3 years from the date of sale by paying delinquent taxes, interest and fees.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary stamp tax when I sell in Douglas County?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, owes $3.32 on each $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026. Whoever presents the deed, buyer or agent, may actually pay it.
